findings.F1: The book fails on its falls, not its gain: it makes 21.0% a year but its deepest fall is −50.6%, so Calmar is 0.42. Its deepest fall episode lasts 426 days across w1–w5 (−46.8%), and the second lasts 440 days across w12–w16 (−40.8%).
findings.F2: The book barely steps aside in its falls. On bars inside its three deepest falls, the coins' 20-day return averaged −1.5% (against +4.9% outside) and the close sat 26.7% below its 60-day high (against 18.7%). The book still held 0.46 of capital (against 0.52) and earned only 0.00018 a bar (against 0.00139).
findings.F3: Volume carries both the gain and the losses. The top volume-ratio quintile has the largest position (0.93) and gain (0.0041 a bar), but also the largest summed losses (−45.6 against −7.4 in the bottom quintile). Inside that quintile the gain is 0.00289 when the 20-day return is negative and 0.00493 when it is positive. The middle quintiles lose in downtrends (−0.00034, −0.00016) and earn in uptrends (0.00072, 0.00102).
findings.F4: The day's direction splits the volume effect over 7 days. In the top volume-ratio tercile, the excess 7-day return is +1.65% after an up day (t 2.18, 399 cases) and −1.01% after a down day (t −1.35, 319 cases). Thin volume after a down day is also followed by −1.51% (t −2.31, 324 cases).
findings.F5: High volume on down days gives only a short bounce. Next-day return after a top-quintile-volume down day is +0.92%, yet the excess over the next 7 days is −1.0%. So the large positions the book takes on heavy-volume selling days pay for one day and then give it back, while the book keeps them for the full week.
findings.F6: The book does best near the coin's high. Bars within 7% of the 60-day high carry the book's highest gain (0.0021 a bar, next-day return +0.25%). Bars more than 22% below it earn near nothing (−0.00002 to 0.0008).

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's traded volume over the past day relative to its average over the past 20 days, the higher its return over the next 7 days, only while the coin's own 20-day return is positive.
ideas.consequence: A volume surge would justify a larger long position over the next week while the coin is rising over the past 20 days, and no position while it is falling, which is when the book's deep falls happen.
ideas.name: volume surge in uptrends

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's traded volume over the past day relative to its average over the past 20 days, the higher its return over the next 7 days, only on days the coin closed above its previous day's close.
ideas.consequence: Heavy volume on a rising day would be a reason to hold the coin long for the week, while heavy volume on a falling day would be a reason to stay out despite its one-day bounce.
ideas.name: volume surge on up days

ideas.idea: The higher a coin's traded volume over the past day relative to its average over the past 20 days, the higher its return over the next 7 days, only while the coin's close is near its 60-day high, with the effect growing the closer the close is to that high.
ideas.consequence: A volume surge close to the recent high would favour a long position for the week, and a surge far below the high would be a reason to stand aside.
ideas.name: volume surge near high
